newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santos port operating normally - port.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santos port operating normally - port.

text.p: Brazil's key port of Santos was working normally after a group of administrative portworkers ended a two-day strike earlier this morning, a CODESP port authority spokeswoman said.
"Already last night there were a few vessels working, then 50 percent of the workers returned to work at 0100 local (0400 GMT) and all ships were operating as of 0700 local this morning," she added.
The workers stopped work at 0100 local on July 1 in protest at not being consulted by CODESP over a switch to 24-hour operations at the port.

However they accepted a suggestion by a Labor Tribunal judge made Wednesday that they return to work while CODESP and union officials negotiate over terms and extra benefits during five working days, the spokeswoman said.
This would be until the end of July 8, she added.
"I think there should be an agreement within five days," the spokeswoman said.
The port was now operating on a 24-hour basis. Some 29 vessels were docked at the port this morning, 24 of which were in public berths. A further 37 were waiting in the bay.
On Wednesday the stoppage had paralyzed all loading and unloading at public berths, hitting sugar, soymeal and possibly coffee loading.
